title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-16
content:
Morning sprint notes - 2026-03-16

High-level:
- Yesterday's canary: 2% of traffic on quant-fused-attn-v2 showed ~6-8% latency tail increase on seq_len=1024. Need triage.
- SRE saw a small bump in p99 GPU utilization on instance pool a3b; suspicious batching behavior around 11:20-11:45 PST.

Today goals:
- Bug triage: reproduce the quant-fused-attn tail with unit tests + microbench. (RW-2387)
- Perf TODOs: add percentile logging to batching layer, validate KV-cache eviction heuristics with long-chat traces.
- Kernel notes: try toggling mixed-precision kernel path and measure against fp16 fallback for seq>=1024.

Notes / observations:
- Symptom: p99 increase only when request mix includes a small percentage (~5%) of long sequences; steady-state throughput unaffected. Hypothesis: bad packing causing oversized batches that force slower attention path.
- Quick check: @Marco ran local microbench: fused-attn-v2 on a single A100 with seq=1024 latency median 78ms, p99 210ms; switching to legacy-fused drops p99 to ~160ms.
- Potential regression introduced by PR GITHUB-PR#3682 that adjusted dynamic tile size selection.

Repro steps (to run locally):
1) checkout pr branch: git fetch && git checkout perf/quant-fused-tune
2) run microbench: ./scripts/bench_attention --model t5-xl --batch 8 --seq 1024 --kernel fused-v2 --iter 200 --profile
3) run same with --kernel fused-v1 and compare p50/p95/p99 (use trace-summary.py)

Immediate actions:
- [ ] Add deterministic unit test that simulates mixed-length traffic (seq 64/256/1024) to repo tests/attention/ (assign to Samira)
- [ ] Roll back dynamic tile selection change on canary cluster and monitor for 48h (assign to SRE)
- [ ] Add percentile emission (p50/p90/p95/p99) in batching debug logs (small perf cost) (assign to me)
- [ ] Run cache eviction sim harness with 10k long-chat traces to validate no thrashing (assign Marco)

Kernel tuning ideas to try this afternoon:
- Force 2-stage KV cache warmup: pre-allocate KV store when sequence length escalates beyond threshold (reduce resizing overhead).
- For seq>=512, pin attention kernel to vectorized path that favors memory locality even if compute slightly higher — tradeoff may reduce tail variability.
- Revisit int8 quantization config: small change in reorder step may break kernel fusion heuristics — try disabling reorder optimization to see if p99 improves.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is this purely kernel-level, or is the runtime batching policy accidentally coalescing very different sequences into one batch? Need to check batching trace UID mapping.
- Does the GPU driver version on canary pool differ from main pool? SRE said same AMI but will confirm kernel driver version.

Debug artifacts / links:
- SRE slack thread: #sre-serving-runtime (see thread ts 2026-03-15T19:12)
- Canary logs (short): s3://redwood-inference/canary/2026-03-15/serving-runtime-logs.tar.gz
- Local microbench script: tools/perf/bench_attention.py

Quick notes to self:
- Keep experiments small and isolated. Use canary flag + sampling so we don't affect customers.
- If kernel patch needed, aim for feature flag hedging so we can revert without redeploying entire runtime.

End-of-day expected deliverables:
- Repro case that demonstrates p99 regression (artifact + steps)
- PR with additional logging + test (small change)
- Recommendation: rollback dynamic tile select on canary if repro confirmed

Random TODOs / low priority:
- Follow up on long-standing TODO: add more descriptive labels to batching spans (span names currently just `batch_dispatch` - add target_seq_len and model_variant).
- Clean up dead code in kernels/legacy_reorder.cpp (refer to TODO comment from 2025-11).

Notes to future me:
- If you hit nondeterministic p99, try increasing microbench iter to 1k to see steady tail behaviour.
- Keep an eye on memory fragmentation metrics; our allocator sometimes causes weird latencies under churn.

End.
